notes: The first show of the run. Eddie Guerrero beats Chris Hero, then trades insults backstage with Chris Benoit, and Paul Heyman books them for Wrestlepalooza on 28 June. Rob Van Dam challenges Raven for the World Heavyweight Championship, Sabu appears wanting the belt too, and the three of them attack one another across the show. Chris Jericho keeps the Television Championship over Lance Storm in the main event. Rated A in the diary, with a counterpart Smackdown rating of B+.

notes: Kurt Angle wins a handicap match against the Hardy Boys when Matt Hardy taps out. notes: The pay-per-view. A triple-header main event: the winners of the seventh and eighth matches are to meet at Summer Assylum for a shot at the world champion, who is decided in the ninth. The Dreamer and Sandman Singapore Cane Match ends in a draw and Rob Van Dam against Sabu ends in a no contest after Van Dam's leap from the second-story guardrail; Stephanie Mcintosh says a rematch will be held on Revolution, and she and Heyman argue over who gets the shot. Raven keeps the World Heavyweight Championship over Goldberg. Rated A* in the diary.

notes: Revolution after Wrestlepalooza. Chris Jericho taunts Cactus Jack after beating him on Friday, Stephanie Mcintosh stops a brawl between Tommy Dreamer and The Sandman and threatens to remove either man from the title picture, and Rey Mysterio Jr. proposes a best-of-seven series with Juventud Guerrera. Rocky beats Cactus Jack in the main event and Cactus smashes himself through a ringside table. The show closes with an ECW Online post that Revolution has offered a contract to a young Canadian, Apocalypse, who trained at the Hart Dungeon. Rated A* in the diary, with a counterpart Raw rating of B.
